title: Disk masses in the Orion Molecular Cloud-2: distinguishing time and environment
question: Are initial disk dust masses in the Orion Molecular Cloud-2 (beyond 0.5 pc from the Trapezium) the same as in low-mass star-forming regions, and how much does external photoevaporation reduce disk masses near the Trapezium?

data.sensitivity: 1 sigma 0.1 mJy/beam in the southern part; 3 sigma dust mass limit 17 Earth masses (32 in the northern part)

what.value: Comparison disk dust mass distributions: Lupus, Taurus, Cham I, Upper Sco, sigma Ori, ONC

evidence.quote: In addition to the regions shown here, the same procedure was also followed for disk masses in Taurus (cite: andrews13) and $\sigma$ Ori (cite: ansdell17).

external_data.citation: Ansdell et al. 2016; Eisner et al. 2018; Barenfeld et al. 2016; Andrews et al. 2013; Ansdell et al. 2017

what.value: Median free-free emission strength and spectral index for correction (0.25 mJy at 3 mm)

evidence.loc: 3.3.2 Contamination by free-free contamination at 3 mm
evidence.quote: we have applied a correction based on the results presented in (cite: tychoniec18) for the median free-free emission strength and spectral index.

what.value: FRIED grid of externally irradiated disk mass-loss rates

evidence.quote: we have also used the FRIED grid of externally irradiated disks (cite: haworth18).

recipe.method: Remove baselines <30 kλ, combine line-free continuum, image with tclean mosaic
key_parameters: uv cut 30 kλ; effective frequency 99.5 GHz

recipe.goal: Measure fluxes at Spitzer YSO positions
recipe.method: Brightest pixel within 2.5'' of catalog position; 3 sigma detection with primary-beam-weighted noise; visual check
peak_local_max on the image, flux in the same 2.5'' aperture, cross-match with other surveys
Optically thin blackbody equation with free-free correction of 0.25 mJy
key_parameters: beta=1, kappa_1000GHz=10 cm2/g, T=20 K (30 K test), d=414 pc

recipe.goal: Disk mass distribution and comparison to other regions
recipe.method: Kaplan-Meier estimator with upper limits; log-rank tests; log-rank with mass scaling factor vs ONC
Compare ratio with Scally & Clarke formula and FRIED grid for fiducial disk
assumptions: Fiducial disk 20 Earth masses, 40 AU, gas-to-dust 100, 0.5 Myr exposure

evidence.quote: Of the disks, 37 are detected by our ALMA observations at at least $3\sigma$, for a detection rate of $28\%$.
26 detections give a detection rate of $69\%$ for these objects.
This sample – the Unidentified point sources – consists of $N=34$ sources.

evidence.loc: 3.2 Disk masses in the OMC-2 field

evidence.quote: This leads to a mass ratio of $0.18^{+0.18}_{-0.11}$ between the regions
we cannot distinguish between the Lupus and OMC-2 disks ($p = 0.87$)
the same is true for the comparison to Taurus ($p = 0.76$)

answer_key.quantity: Log-rank p-value OMC-2 vs Cham I

answer_key.value: 8e-8 (abstract); 1e-8 from observations vs 8e-8 from Scally & Clarke

evidence.quote: our observations imply a photoevaporative mass loss rate of $1 \times 10^{-8}\,M_{\odot}\,\text{yr}^{-1}$ in the ONC.

not_stated_but_needed: tclean weighting/robust, cell size, image size, niter, threshold and masks
Which spectral ranges were excluded as line-contaminated
Calibration details (CASA version of calibration, pipeline vs manual) and flux scale uncertainty
peak_local_max parameters (threshold, min distance) for the unidentified source search
Exact log-rank and Kaplan-Meier implementation, including the mass-scaling fit procedure for the 0.18 ratio
Dust mass conversion detail: how flux was scaled from 99.5 GHz and the free-free subtraction per source
missing_for_reproduction: Imaging parameters (weighting, cell, size, masks, threshold)
score_reason: Public data and a clear simple method, but imaging parameters and the statistical procedure are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple flux extraction and mass conversion with numeric results; imaging details need choices.
